title: Late Report Penalty Limits by Employer Size (Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts)
content:
**Rule applied at the desk.** On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, the limit applied to the multiplied late report penalty amount follows the highest monthly employee count on the report — the highest of the three monthly counts on the original report the penalty is worked out from:

- a report showing at least 50 is limited by the large employer cap of USD 1000.00;
- a report showing at least the electronic filing threshold of 10 but fewer than 50 is limited by the mid-size employer cap of USD 500.00;
- a report showing fewer than 10 is limited by the class's late report penalty maximum.

The electronic filing threshold is 10 employees in every financing class.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical reports)

- **Counts of 48, 51 and 49.** The highest is 51, at least 50: limit USD 1000.00.
- **Counts of 50, 50 and 50.** The highest is exactly 50, which is "at least 50": limit USD 1000.00.
- **Counts of 47, 49 and 46.** The highest is 49, fewer than 50 but at least 10: limit USD 500.00.
- **Counts of 8, 10 and 9.** The highest is exactly 10, at the threshold: limit USD 500.00.
- **Counts of 9, 9 and 7.** The highest is 9, fewer than 10: the class's late report penalty maximum is the limit.
- **Which month decides.** Only the highest of the three months matters; a report whose first two months show 12 and 15 employees and whose third shows 52 is limited at USD 1000.00.

**Illustration.** A multiplied amount of USD 1080.00 on a report whose highest monthly count is 62 is limited to USD 1000.00; the same amount on a report whose highest count is 30 is limited to USD 500.00.
